text:
1. If the pot size given for a plant is not a whole number of centimetres of at least 5 and at most 60 (width across the top of the pot, in whole centimetres), the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
   Reason: Builder's limit: 5 to 60 cm across the top, whole centimetres. Refuse rather than round, as the builder asked.
   Check: test. Pass: for each size the part refuses with the pot size named as wrong and the reason, and changes nothing; sizes equal to each bound are accepted. Conditions: sizes 4, 5, 60, 61, 0, -3, 12.5, 'abc'.

2. The part shall run on the user's Linux laptop.
   Reason: Builder: used on a Linux laptop at home.
   Check: demonstration. Pass: the builder sees the part start on their laptop and carry out adding a plant and showing the plants to water today. Conditions: builder's own laptop, a throwaway copy of the data.

3. If the place given for a plant is anything other than inside or on the balcony, the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
   Reason: Builder: 'Inside or on the balcony. Nothing else.' Two values are all the rain rule can use.
   Check: test. Pass: for each value other than the two allowed, the part refuses naming the place as wrong; 'inside' and 'balcony' are accepted. Conditions: values 'garden', 'Inside ' (trailing space), empty, 'balcony'.

4. When the user gives new details for a plant on the list that each meet the limits for a plant and confirms the change, the part shall replace that plant's details with the new ones.
   Reason: The function itself.
   Check: test. Pass: afterwards the list shows the new details for that plant, and other plants are unchanged. Conditions: a plant with 2 logged waterings; change its place and interval.

5. When the user confirms the removal of a watering logged for a plant on a day, the part shall take that watering out of the plant's record.
   Reason: The function itself: a watering logged by mistake would make a plant look watered and drop it from the plan; the plant's clock then counts from the latest remaining watering.
   Check: test. Pass: the plant's history no longer shows the day, other days are unchanged, and the plant's due day is worked out from its latest remaining watering. Conditions: plant with 3 waterings; remove the latest.

6. When the user asks to change a plant, the part shall show the plant's current details and the new details and change nothing until the user confirms.
   Reason: Builder chose to respond to a change made by mistake with a confirmation, no undo. Assumes that 'changed' covers a change of details as well as removal.
   Check: test. Pass: before confirmation both sets of details are shown and the list is unchanged; after the user declines the list is still unchanged; after confirming it holds the new details. Conditions: one plant; a change requested; three runs: no answer, decline, confirm.

7. When the part is started again after being closed, the part shall hold every plant that was on the list when it was closed, with the four details as last left and the day it was added.
   Reason: The plant list goes to functions that run on a later day (list, plan, history); builder does not want to retype it. The added day is kept because a plant never watered is first due that day.
   Check: test. Pass: the list after restart equals, plant for plant and detail for detail, the list before closing, and a plant added 5 days ago and never watered is still due today after the restart. Conditions: a list after adding 3 plants, changing one and removing one; part closed and started again.

8. If no plant is named for removal, or the named plant is not on the list, the part shall refuse it, say which plant could not be found, and change nothing.
   Reason: A removal of nothing cannot be carried out; the builder wants refusals to say why and change nothing.
   Check: test. Pass: the part refuses naming the plant it could not find and the list is unchanged. Conditions: plant name not on the list; plant name left out.

9. While the home town is set and at least one plant is on the list, if no plant is due today, the part shall tell the user that no plant needs water today.
   Reason: An empty list can read as a failure; the builder dislikes an empty screen.
   Check: test. Pass: the part states that no plant needs water today instead of an empty output. Conditions: plants on the list, none due.

10. If adding a plant would leave the list with more than 60 plants (number of plants on the list, at most 60), the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Builder: at most 60 plants; about 40 now. Refused rather than dropped, as the builder asked.
    Check: test. Pass: with the list at the maximum of 60, adding one more plant is refused with the reason, and the list is unchanged; with one fewer than the maximum, adding succeeds. Conditions: lists of 59 and 60 plants made from throwaway data.

11. When the user gives a plant on the list and a day that meets the limits, the part shall record that the plant was watered on that day, so that the plant's schedule counts from the latest logged day.
    Reason: The function itself: the plan counts from the last watering, so logging is what resets the clock. 'Counts from the latest' covers logging an earlier day after a later one.
    Check: test. Pass: the plant's history shows the day, and a plant that would have been due today is not due today after logging today's date. Conditions: a plant due today; log today.

12. If the day given for a watering is a day after today, or is earlier than today by more than 1 year (how long before today the day lies, at most 1 year), the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Builder: today or any earlier day up to a year back, never a day to come.
    Check: test. Pass: tomorrow and the day before the same date a year back are refused naming the day as wrong; today and the same date a year back are accepted (the edge is asked of the builder; proof updated when settled). Conditions: dates computed from today for tomorrow, today, same date one year back, the day before that.

13. The part shall show at the top of the plants to water today the home town and the day the forecast was asked for.
    Reason: Builder chose to respond to a forecast that does not match their weather: see at the top which town and day.
    Check: test. Pass: the first lines of the output name the home town and today's date, with and without a usable forecast. Conditions: home town set; forecast good, then not obtained.

14. If the town name given is not between 1 and 60 characters long (number of characters in the town name as given, at least 1 and at most 60), the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Builder: up to 60 characters, never blank. Whether the forecast service knows the town is not checked here: see the rule for a wrong or missing forecast answer.
    Check: test. Pass: towns of length 0 and 61 characters are refused naming the town as wrong and the home town is unchanged; lengths 1 and 60 are accepted. Conditions: a home town already set; towns of length 0, 1, 60, 61.

15. When the user asks to remove a plant, the part shall show which plant it would remove and remove nothing until the user confirms.
    Reason: Builder chose to respond: show what will be removed and ask to confirm; no undo.
    Check: test. Pass: before confirmation the plant to be removed is named and still on the list; after the user declines it is still on the list; after confirming it is gone. Conditions: one plant; removal requested; runs: no answer, decline, confirm.

16. If the forecast was not obtained, the part shall treat rain as not expected today, so that every plant due by its own schedule is on the plants due today.
    Reason: Builder: go by each plant's own schedule as if no rain were coming. Leaving a due balcony plant off is the worse error.
    Check: test. Pass: balcony plants due today appear on the plants due today when the stand-in service does not answer and when it answers wrongly. Conditions: balcony plant due today; stand-in service silent, then answering 600 mm.

17. When the user confirms the removal of a plant on the list, the part shall take that plant off the list so that it is no longer listed and no longer planned for.
    Reason: The function itself: a plant given away must stop being listed or planned for, or it is watered for nothing. What happens to the plant's logged waterings is not settled: asked of the builder.
    Check: test. Pass: after confirming, the list does not show the plant and the plants to water today does not include it even though it was due; other plants are unchanged. Conditions: a plant that is due today; remove it.

18. The part shall put on the plants due today every plant that is due today, except a balcony plant whose due day is today while rain is expected today.
    Reason: Builder: a plant that is due must never be left off by mistake: prevent. Rain excuses only a plant due today, not one already late. Holds for every combination of place, due state and rain.
    Check: test. Pass: for every combination in the conditions, the plants due today equal exactly the plants counted due except the excused ones; no due plant outside the exception is missing. Conditions: every combination of place (inside, balcony), due state (not due, due today, overdue, never watered and added earlier), forecast (no rain, rain at the threshold, forecast not obtained). The set of combinations is small and fully listable, so a test can check all of them.

19. When the user gives a name, a pot size, a watering interval and a place that each meet the limits for a plant, and the list can take another plant, the part shall add a plant with exactly those four details to the list.
    Reason: The function itself: a plant that is not on the list can never be planned for, so adding is the way every plant gets its schedule.
    Check: test. Pass: after adding, asking for the list shows a plant with exactly the name, pot size, interval and place given, and no other plant changed. Conditions: a list of 3 plants; one new plant with valid details.

20. The part shall put on the plants due today only plants that are due today.
    Reason: Result of the function; a plant listed that is not due is overwatered.
    Check: test. Pass: for every combination, no plant appears that is not counted due. Conditions: every combination of place (inside, balcony), due state (not due, due today, overdue, never watered and added earlier), forecast (no rain, rain at the threshold, not obtained); the case controls today's date.

21. While the forecast was not obtained, the part shall tell the user that the forecast could not be used and that the plants shown are those due by their own schedule.
    Reason: Builder: be told the forecast could not be used.
    Check: test. Pass: the output states the forecast could not be used and that the list is by schedule alone; with a good forecast it does not. Conditions: stand-in service silent; then answering well.

22. If the watering interval given for a plant is not a whole number of days from 1 to 60 (days between waterings the plant likes, as a whole number, at least 1 and at most 60), the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Builder's limit: every 1 to 60 days, whole days.
    Check: test. Pass: for each value the part refuses with the interval named as wrong and why, and changes nothing; values equal to each bound are accepted. Conditions: values 0, 1, 60, 61, -1, 2.5, 'weekly'.

23. When the user asks for the list of plants, the part shall show every plant on the list with its name, pot size, watering interval and place as last left.
    Reason: The function itself: the user reads the list to see what the part holds; 'as last left' ties it to earlier additions, changes and removals.
    Check: test. Pass: every plant of the list appears once with its four details equal to those last entered, after additions, changes and removals; no removed plant appears. Conditions: a list of 40 plants after 5 changes and 3 removals.

24. If no plant is named for a history, or the named plant is not on the list, the part shall say which plant could not be found.
    Reason: Unknown input is answered, not ignored.
    Check: test. Pass: the part names what could not be found and shows no history. Conditions: plant not on the list; plant left out.

25. The part shall give each plant due today an amount of water equal to 10 ml/cm for each centimetre of its pot size, rounded to the nearest 10 ml.
    Reason: Builder: about 10 ml per centimetre, nearest 10 ml: a 15 cm pot gets 150 ml. With whole centimetres the rounding changes nothing.
    Check: test. Pass: a 5, 15 and 60 cm pot get 50, 150 and 600 ml, consistent with 10 ml per centimetre. Conditions: three plants due today with those pots.

26. When the plants to water today are asked for, the part shall ask the forecast service for today's weather in the home town and take from the answer whether rain is expected today.
    Reason: The function itself: the plan needs rain information; the builder does not want to check the weather.
    Check: test, needing a stand-in forecast service so that the request can be seen; the real one cannot be controlled. Pass: the stand-in service receives one request naming the home town and today, and the part's answer to rain follows what the stand-in replied. Conditions: stand-in service answering 0 mm and 10 mm; home town 'Haifa'.

27. If a watering is already logged for the given plant on the given day, the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Builder: a plant can be logged once per day.
    Check: test. Pass: the part refuses saying it is already logged, and the plant's history is unchanged; the same day for another plant is accepted. Conditions: two plants; log plant 1 on a day twice, then plant 2 on that day.

28. While a plant has no logged watering, when the user asks for its watering history, the part shall tell the user that none is logged for that plant.
    Reason: An empty answer reads as a fault.
    Check: test. Pass: the part states no watering is logged for that plant. Conditions: a newly added plant.

29. While no home town is set or no plant is on the list, when the user opens the part, the part shall tell the user which of the town and the plants still have to be entered, and not show a watering plan.
    Reason: Builder: not an empty screen or an error, tell me what to do first. The plan is held back because it cannot be made without both.
    Check: test. Pass: with nothing set the output names both the town and the plants; with only one missing it names that one; with both set it names neither. Conditions: four states: nothing set; town only; plants only; both.

30. If no plant is named for a change, or the named plant is not on the list, the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Input 'which plant' is the user's; a change to a plant that is not there cannot be applied.
    Check: test. Pass: the part refuses, says which plant could not be found, and the list is unchanged. Conditions: plant name not on the list; plant name left out.

31. If the name given for a plant is not between 1 and 40 characters long (number of characters in the name as given, at least 1 and at most 40), the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Builder's limit: up to 40 characters, never blank; refusing and naming the fault was the builder's choice over quietly fixing it.
    Check: test. Pass: for each name, the part refuses, the message names the name as the wrong detail and says why, and the list and waterings are identical to before. A name of exactly the minimum and exactly the maximum is accepted. Conditions: names: empty, one character below and above each bound (lengths 0, 1, 40, 41), and 200 characters. Boundary values are exact and the refusal is observable; a program can check every boundary on each change.

32. If the plant named for removal of a watering is not on the list, or no watering is logged for that plant on the given day, or either is left out, the part shall refuse it, say which was not found, and change nothing.
    Reason: Refusals say why and change nothing.
    Check: test. Pass: the part refuses naming what could not be found and no record changes. Conditions: unknown plant; day with no watering; day left out.

33. If the name given for a new plant is the name of a plant already on the list, the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Builder: no two plants with the same name, or they cannot be told apart. Whether 'Fern' and 'fern' are the same name is not settled: asked of the builder.
    Check: test. Pass: the part refuses, names the name as the wrong detail and says it is already on the list, and the list is unchanged. Conditions: a list with a plant named 'Fern'; a new plant named exactly 'Fern'. Names differing in case are not part of this proof until the builder settles it.

34. The part shall show beside each plant shown in the plants to water today the day of its last logged watering, or that it was never watered.
    Reason: Builder chose to respond to a plant being listed that does not need water: see the last watering and check the soil.
    Check: test. Pass: each plant shown in the plants to water today has the latest logged day beside it, or 'never watered' when none is logged. Conditions: two plants due today: one with 2 waterings long enough ago to be due, one never watered.

35. When the user gives a town name that meets its limits, the part shall take it as the home town.
    Reason: The function itself: without a town the forecast cannot be asked for and no plan is made.
    Check: test. Pass: after giving a town the forecast request names that town; giving a second town replaces the first. Conditions: stand-in service; town 'Haifa', then 'Eilat'. Seen in the request the stand-in forecast service receives; a program checks it on every change.

36. The part shall work out the plants due today from the plants, waterings and forecast as they are when the plants to water today are asked for.
    Reason: A plan from before a logged watering, a removed entry or a changed plant would list a watered plant or miss a due one.
    Check: test. Pass: after each of logging today's watering, removing a watering, changing an interval, removing a plant, the plants due today is: after logging today, the plant absent; after removing that watering, the plant present again; after changing the interval to 60, the plant absent; after removing the plant, absent. Conditions: one plant with interval 3 last watered 3 days ago (a controlled date), forecast 0 mm; each step is made, then the plan asked for, in turn.

37. The part shall count a plant as due today when the days from its last logged watering to today are at least its watering interval, or, when it has no logged watering, when today is the day it was added or a later day.
    Reason: Builder: a plant never watered is first due the day it is added; 'every N days' read as due N days after the last watering (assumed). 'Today' is the date of the computer's clock; assumed.
    Check: test. Pass: with rain not expected, the plants to water today are exactly: the interval-3 plant last watered 3 days ago and the one last watered 4 days ago, the plant added today, and the plant added 5 days ago; the plants last watered 1 and 2 days ago are not listed. Conditions: the case controls today's date. Plants with interval 3 last watered 1, 2, 3, 4 days ago; a plant added today; one added 5 days ago never watered; forecast 0 mm.

38. If the forecast service has not answered within 10 s (longest time from asking to giving up, at most 10 s), the part shall stop waiting and treat the forecast as not obtained.
    Reason: Builder: wait up to 10 seconds, then go on without it.
    Check: test. Pass: the part stops waiting no later than 10 s after asking, and reports the forecast as not obtained. Conditions: stand-in service that accepts the request and never replies; the case measures the time to give up with a clock accurate to 0.1 s and allows no more than 0.5 s over 10 s for the part's own work.

39. When the part is started again after being closed, the part shall hold every watering that was logged and not removed when it was closed, with its plant and day.
    Reason: Builder wants the record of waterings to be there tomorrow.
    Check: test. Pass: every plant's history after restart equals its history before closing. Conditions: 3 plants with several waterings each, one entry removed; closed and started again.

40. If the new details of a plant would leave it with a name, pot size, watering interval or place that a new plant could not be given, or with the name of another plant on the list, the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: A change must not get around the limits the builder set for plants; same response as for a new plant. Whether a plant keeping its own name counts as a duplicate is asked of the builder.
    Check: test. Pass: each change is refused naming the wrong detail and why, and plant, list and waterings are as before. Conditions: a list of two plants; changes to: name over limit, pot 61, interval 0, place 'garden', name of the other plant.

41. If the forecast service answers with no rain figure for today, or with a rain figure that is not between 0 and 500 mm (a rain figure the part may use, at least 0 and at most 500), the part shall treat the forecast as not obtained.
    Reason: Builder: such an answer counts as wrong, the same as no answer.
    Check: test. Pass: answers with no rain figure, -0.1 mm, 500.1 mm and a non-number are treated as not obtained; 0 and 500 mm are used. Conditions: stand-in service returning each of these answers.

42. If the name, the pot size, the watering interval or the place is not given for a new plant, the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Builder: leave one out and it is refused and named. A plant with a missing detail cannot be scheduled.
    Check: test. Pass: in each of four runs, leaving out one detail, the part refuses, names the missing detail, and the list is unchanged. Conditions: otherwise valid details, one of the four left out each time.

43. When the user asks for the plants to water today, the part shall show each plant due today with its name and its amount of water.
    Reason: The function itself: the user waters from this list, so each plant must appear with the amount to give.
    Check: test. Pass: each plant due today appears once with its name and amount. Conditions: 3 plants due today with different pots.

44. When the part is started again after being closed, the part shall hold the home town that was set when it was closed.
    Reason: The town goes to functions that run on a later morning (no retyping).
    Check: test. Pass: after restart the forecast request names the town set before closing. Conditions: stand-in service; town set, part closed and started again.

45. If no plant is named for a watering, or the named plant is not on the list, or no day is given, the part shall refuse it, say which detail is wrong and why, and change nothing.
    Reason: Missing or unknown input is refused with the reason.
    Check: test. Pass: in each case the part refuses naming what is missing or unknown and no watering is recorded. Conditions: plant left out; plant not on the list; day left out.

46. When the user asks to remove a watering, the part shall show the plant and the day of the watering it would remove and remove nothing until the user confirms.
    Reason: Builder chose to respond with a confirmation, no undo.
    Check: test. Pass: before confirmation the plant and day are named and the watering is still recorded; after declining it is still recorded; after confirming it is gone. Conditions: one plant, one watering; runs: no answer, decline, confirm.

47. When the user asks for the watering history of a plant on the list, the part shall show each day the plant was watered, as logged.
    Reason: The function itself: the user checks the days to find a watering logged by mistake.
    Check: test. Pass: the days shown equal the logged days for that plant, after additions and removals of waterings, and no other plant's. Conditions: two plants with different waterings; one entry removed.

48. If the forecast service cannot be reached, or answers with an error or with something that is not a number for the rain figure, the part shall treat the forecast as not obtained.
    Reason: Builder: no answer or a wrong answer is handled the same way; a refused connection or error would otherwise show the user a failure instead of the plan.
    Check: test, needing a service made to fail at once, which a real one cannot be made to do on demand. Pass: with each failure the part reports the forecast as not obtained and goes on to the plan without waiting. Conditions: stand-in service: connection refused; error status; answer 'abc' for the rain figure; no network.

49. The part shall take rain as expected today if and only if the total rain figure of today's forecast for the whole day is at least 2 mm.
    Reason: Builder: 2 mm or more is rain, less is a drizzle and the plants stay dry.
    Check: test. Pass: seen through a balcony plant due today: it is left off the plants to water today for 2.0 and 10 mm and is on them for 0 and 1.9 mm. Conditions: stand-in service returning 0, 1.9, 2.0, 10 mm for the day's total; one balcony plant due today.

Left open

1. Are "Fern" and "fern" the same name for the no-duplicates rule?
2. Are names or towns of only spaces blank?
3. When a plant is removed, do its logged waterings go with it?
4. When a plant is changed, do its waterings stay, and does keeping its own name count as a duplicate?
5. Is the day exactly one year back accepted when logging a watering?
6. Is a plant due N days after its last watering for an interval of N, with "today" taken from the laptop's date? (The author wrote this as a firm rule, so it is still waiting on the answer.)
7. If the part is stopped mid-save, do you want either the old or the new state and never a mix?
8. Should changing a plant ask for confirmation, as removing does?
9. If the town isn't one the forecast service knows, is that "forecast not usable"?
10. If the stored data can't be read at start, should the part refuse to start rather than carry on as if nothing were set up?
11. When you confirm a request, is it checked before or after?
12. The hazard of losing the only copy of your data is accepted but needs an issue for synthesis. The project has no GitHub remote, so should it be recorded another way?
13. Should "comfortable in a terminal" and "you install and maintain it yourself" be requirements, out of scope, or left to synthesis?

1. If the service gives no answer within 10 seconds, or gives an answer without a rain figure, or with a rain figure below 0 or above 500 mm, the forecast is not used. The product tells the user the forecast could not be used and lists every plant due by its own schedule, balcony plants too, as if no rain was coming. A rain figure of exactly 0 or exactly 500 is usable.
   Check: test with a stubbed service, where a balcony plant is due today and the same plant would be excused by 5 mm. The cases are: no reply (hang forever); reply after 9 s (usable, used); reply after 11 s; reply with HTTP error; reply that is not readable; reply with no rain figure; -0.1; 500.1; 0; 500. Pass when, for each unusable case, the user is told the forecast could not be used, the balcony plant and all other due plants are listed, and the answer arrives within 11 s of starting. For 0 and 500 the forecast is used. Also run with the network disconnected.

2. A balcony plant that is due today and not overdue is left off the plants to water today when the usable forecast says rain. It is listed when the forecast says no rain. A plant is overdue on any day after its due day.
   Check: test with a stubbed forecast. A balcony plant with interval 7, last watered 7 days ago, so due today, is not listed with 5 mm and is listed with 0 mm. The same plant last watered 8 days ago (overdue) is listed with 5 mm. A never-watered balcony plant added today is not listed with 5 mm. A never-watered plant added yesterday is listed with 5 mm.

3. No two plants on the list have the same name. Adding a plant, or changing a plant's name, to a name another plant already has is refused. Changing a plant's other details while keeping its own name is not a clash.
   Check: test. Add 'Fern'. Adding a second 'Fern' is refused. Add 'Ivy', then rename 'Ivy' to 'Fern': refused, 'Ivy' unchanged. Change the pot size of 'Fern' leaving its name: accepted. Remove 'Fern', then add 'Fern' again: accepted (the name is free once the plant is gone). Case check: 'fern' against 'Fern' follows the assumption (see Left open).

4. Whenever something the user enters is outside its limits, missing, or names a plant or entry that is not there, the product refuses it, says which entry is wrong and why, and changes nothing. It does not round, trim, cut or otherwise correct the entry. When several entries are wrong, all are named.
   Check: test over every action that takes input (add, change, remove plant, log, remove entry, set town, history lookup). For each, send one case per rule above, a missing entry, an entry naming an unknown plant, and a case with two wrong entries. Pass when each refusal names every wrong entry with a reason; the stored data is identical before and after; no value was altered (12.5 is not stored as 12, a 41-character name is not stored cut to 40).

5. Each time the plants to water today are worked out, the product asks an online forecast service for today's weather in the home town and takes the expected rain from the answer. The user never types in the weather. Only the town name is sent to the service.
   Check: test plus demonstration plus inspection. Test with a stubbed service: it receives one request carrying the set town and nothing about plants, and its rain figure appears in the result. Change the town and run again: the stub receives the new town (no earlier answer is reused). Demonstration: once, against the real service, with the user's real town, from the user's laptop; the shown figures match the service's own page. Inspection: no input anywhere in the product accepts a weather value.

6. Removing a logged watering takes that day out of the plant's record, and the last watering and the schedule then count from the latest day that is left (or from the day the plant was added, when none is left).
   Check: test, interval 7. Log 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-10. Remove 2026-11-10 (confirmed). History shows only 2026-11-01 and the plant's last watering is 2026-11-01. Remove the other too: the plant is treated as never watered. Removing an entry that is not in the record is refused.

7. Where a plant lives is either 'inside' or 'on the balcony' and nothing else. This holds when a plant is added and when it is changed.
   Check: test through Add and through Change. 'inside' and 'balcony' are accepted. 'garden', 'outside' and empty are refused, naming the location as wrong; nothing is stored or changed.

8. Logging a watering adds that day to the plant's record. The plant's last watering is its latest logged day, and the plant's schedule counts from it. Logging an earlier day than the latest does not move the last watering back.
   Check: test, interval 7, today 2026-11-15. Log 2026-11-10: due on 2026-11-17, not before. Log 2026-11-15: due 2026-11-22. Then log 2026-11-01: last watering is still 2026-11-15, due date unchanged.

9. Rain means a forecast of 2 mm or more for the day. Less than 2 mm is not rain.
   Check: test with a stubbed forecast and a balcony plant due today. 1.9 mm: listed. 2.0 mm: not listed. 2.1 mm: not listed. 0 mm: listed.

10. Looking up a plant shows each day it was watered, as logged. A plant with none says so. An unknown plant is refused.
    Check: test. Log 3 days for plant A and 1 for B. A's history shows exactly its 3 days, B's shows 1. A plant with none shows an explicit 'no waterings logged'. Lookup of a plant not on the list is refused. Plants with 365 logged days show all of them.

11. Every plant that is due by the rules for when a plant is due, for rain excusing a balcony plant due today, and for when the forecast cannot be used is on the plants to water today. report:
**Report**

**Coverage.** Both sets cover every function and hazard. The only exception is HAZ-5MGY, which the owner accepted, so neither set needs a requirement for it. X handles this better. It splits persistence into separate requirements for plants with their added day (7), waterings (39) and the town (44). It also states the never-watered rule and the rain exception as exact rules (37 and 18). X keeps "which day is due" and "rain excuses" apart, so each can be tested alone. Y covers the same ground with fewer, bigger requirements. Several of those bundle many clauses, such as Y1, Y4 and Y15.

**Faithfulness.** This is the main difference. Y states several things as settled that the inputs never say:
- Y13 and Y26 say a name or town of only spaces is blank. X leaves this open.
- Y3 says keeping a plant's own name when changing it is not a clash. X leaves this open.
- Y21 says a removed plant's waterings go with it, and Y15 makes the prompt state how many. X leaves the first open.
- Y28 fixes a leap-day rule for "a year back". X leaves the edge open.
- Y18 requires each change to be saved as it is made, and the test kills the process abruptly. X leaves this open (item 7).
- Y33 requires first-use text that names the data folder, and Y5 requires that only the town is sent to the service. Neither comes from the inputs.
- Y27 turns "comfortable in a terminal" into install and no-background-process rules. X leaves that to synthesis.

Some of these appear in Y's Left open list, but the requirement text still states them as firm, so they are inconsistent. X marks its uncertain points in the checks and in Left open. Its main flaw is that X12 and X37 state a rule firmly while also listing it as open.

**Checks.** X's checks are concrete and cheap, and most use boundary values. Y's checks are strong in places, such as the timing cases. Others cost more than they need to, such as 10,000 random states, time-zone runs and a rounding test on 12.5 cm.

**Restraint.** X is wordier, but it invents less. Y adds extras that nobody asked for.

{"verdict": "X", "reason": "X keeps to the inputs and marks unsettled points as open, while Y states several unsettled or invented rules as firm (blank-by-spaces, own-name clash, waterings removed with the plant, save-on-every-change, folder text)."}

**Report: X compared with Y**

**Coverage.** X covers every function and every hazard.
- Persistence, with each change saved as it is made, answers the lost-data loss and the accepted "copy the folder" choice (X18, X33).
- Never leaving a due plant off is handled by X11, a property test, with a fixed 60-plant case that must not be cut off by paging.
- Confirmation before removing a plant or a watering, or before changing a plant, is X15.
- Last-watered dates and the town and day header are X25 and X34.

Y covers most of the same ground. It has no checks for multiple wrong entries, name reuse after removal, or removing a plant together with its waterings. Y also has no requirement that persistence be immediate.

**Faithfulness.** Both mostly stay within the inputs.
- X settles a few details the owner never gave: "nothing runs in background" (X27), the leap-day rule (X28) and the 365-day history (X10). X lists the leap-day rule under Left open, and X27 is a mild addition. X also sends only the town name to the service (X5), which is a sensible privacy choice.
- Y flags its assumptions in Left open but is looser. It states "due N days after last watering" firmly (Y37) even though its own Left open item 6 asks about it.

**Clarity.** Y's one-behaviour EARS style is tidy, but "say which detail is wrong and why" is repeated generically. X defines "overdue" explicitly (X2), states the boundaries exactly (X1, X9), and names all wrong entries together (X4).

**Checks.** X's checks are concrete: stubbed forecast values, a settable clock, time-zone cases and a byte-identical comparison of stored data. The 10,000-state property check is expensive but justified by the hazard. Y's checks are adequate but thinner. Y's rain check (Y49) and timing check (Y38) are good.

**Restraint.** X is long and has some overlap between requirements, for example X4 against the individual validation rules. Y's Left open list includes project-process items (a GitHub issue, terminal comfort) that are noise for builders.

Overall X is the stronger set.

{"verdict": "X", "reason": "X covers every function and hazard with exact, concrete checks and flags its assumptions as open, while Y leaves gaps (multi-error refusals, name reuse, immediate saving) and has thinner checks."}

1. Statement: If the name given for a new plant is the same as the name of a plant already on the list, then the part shall refuse the request, tell the user which entry is wrong and why, and change nothing that is stored. Reason: The builder tells plants apart only by name, so two plants with one name would make every watering log and removal ambiguous. Check: test. Pass: the part refuses with a message that names the name as wrong because it is already used, and the list still holds exactly one plant. Conditions: a list holding a plant named Fern; try to add a second plant named Fern with all other details valid.

2. Statement: When the user gives new details for a plant on the list, and none of them would be refused for a new plant (a name identical to the plant's own current name is not a duplicate), the part shall replace the details given and keep the plant's other details and its logged waterings. Reason: A plant that changes place or needs another interval is the same plant with the same history; replacing it by a new one would lose its waterings, part of the record the builder fears to lose. A change that keeps the own name must pass, or no other detail could be changed. Check: test. Pass: after each change the plant holds the new detail, every other detail is as before, and both waterings are still logged for the plant; neither request is refused. Conditions: a plant Fern, 15 cm, every 7 days, inside, with two waterings logged; change only the interval to 10; then change only the place to balcony and give the name Fern again.

3. Statement: When the user asks to see the list of plants, the part shall show every plant on the list with its name, pot size, how often it likes water and where it lives. Reason: The user needs to check that the list matches the plants they own. Every plant, because a plant missing from the view looks like a plant removed. Check: test. Pass: the output holds 40 plants and for each the four details exactly as entered. Conditions: a list of 40 plants with distinct names, mixed places and sizes.

4. Statement: If the user asks for the waterings of a plant that is not on the list, then the part shall tell the user that the plant is not on the list. Reason: Showing an empty history for a name that does not exist would look like a plant never watered; a wrong spelling must be visible. Check: test. Pass: the part says Moss is not on the list and shows no history. Conditions: a list holding Fern; ask for the waterings of Moss.

5. Statement: When no plant is due today, the part shall tell the user that no plant is to be watered today. Reason: An empty screen after opening cannot be told from a part that failed, and a user who doubts it would water by guess. Check: test. Pass: the output says no plant is to be watered today. Conditions: one plant watered today, home town set, no rain.

6. Statement: When the user asks to remove a watering entry, the part shall show the plant and the day of the entry and ask the user to confirm, and remove nothing until the user confirms. Reason: The builder chose confirmation over an undo for a watering removed by mistake, since the record is hard to rebuild from memory. Check: test. Pass: each time the part shows Fern and the day of the entry and asks for confirmation; after the no, and after closing, both waterings are held. Conditions: plant Fern with two waterings; ask to remove one and answer no; ask again and close the part without answering.

7. Statement: While a forecast was used for the plants to water today, the part shall show above the list the home town and the day the forecast was for. Reason: The builder wants to see at once when the forecast does not fit: the wrong town or an old day. Check: test. Pass: the first lines of the output, before any plant, name Bergen and today's date. Conditions: home town Bergen, today fixed, stand-in forecast answering; open the part.

8. Statement: If the forecast service answers with an answer the part cannot read, with no rainfall figure for today, or with a figure outside 0 to 500 mm, then the part shall treat the forecast as not obtained. Reason: The builder counts a missing or impossible figure as no answer: a rain figure below 0 or above 500 mm cannot be true, and planning from it could wrongly excuse a plant from water. Check: test. Pass: for each bad answer the forecast is treated as not obtained (the plan lists the balcony plant and says the forecast could not be used); the controls are used. Conditions: a stand-in forecast service answering with an unreadable body; an answer with no rainfall figure; a figure one below 0; a figure one above 500; controls: exactly 0 and exactly 500; balcony plant due today.

9. Statement: If the pot size given for a plant is left out, is not a whole number of centimetres, or is outside 5 to 60 cm, then the part shall refuse the request, tell the user which entry is wrong and why, and change nothing that is stored. Reason: The amount of water comes from the pot width, so a wrong width gives a wrong amount, and too much water is what rots roots. The range and the whole-centimetre rule are the builder's. Check: test. Pass: each of the four bad tries is refused naming the pot size and the reason, and the list is unchanged; both controls are added. Conditions: try to add a plant, all else valid, with a pot size of nothing; 12.5; 4; 61; controls: exactly 5 and exactly 60.

10. Statement: If the user asks to remove a plant that is not on the list, then the part shall refuse the request, tell the user which entry is wrong and why, and change nothing that is stored. Reason: Answering a removal of an unknown name with success would let a mistyped name pass as done while the wanted plant stays. Refusal follows the builder's rule for entries that are wrong. Check: test. Pass: the part refuses naming the plant as not on the list, and the list still holds Fern. Conditions: a list holding Fern; ask to remove Moss.

11. Statement: When the part shows a plant to water today, the part shall show beside it the day the plant was last watered, or that it has never been watered. Reason: The builder prefers to see the last watering and feel the soil before pouring; this is how a plant that does not need water, or one that has had enough, is noticed. Check: test. Pass: the line of the first plant holds the day 9 days ago, and the line of the second says it has never been watered. Conditions: two plants due today: one last watered 9 days ago, one never watered.

12. Statement: If the day given for a watering is left out, is later than today, or is more than a number of days (to be decided) before today, then the part shall refuse the request, tell the user which entry is wrong and why, and change nothing that is stored. Reason: A day to come would push a plant's due day into the future and hide a plant that is due, which is the loss the builder fears most. The builder allows today and any earlier day up to a year back. Check: test. Pass: each bad try is refused naming the day and the reason, and nothing is stored; both controls are stored. Conditions: plant Fern; log a watering with no day; tomorrow; the day one beyond the upper bound before today; controls: today and exactly the upper bound before today.

13. Statement: When the user gives a plant on the list and a valid day, the part shall add that day to the plant's logged waterings. Reason: The plant's schedule counts from the latest logged watering, so an unlogged watering means a plant flagged due that was just watered, and too much water. Check: test. Pass: Fern's logged waterings are exactly those two days. Conditions: plant Fern; log a watering for Fern today and one for 10 days ago.

14. Statement: If the user asks to remove a watering entry for a plant and day that has no logged watering, then the part shall refuse the request, tell the user which entry is wrong and why, and change nothing that is stored. Reason: Answering success for an entry that does not exist would let a mistyped day pass while the wrong entry stays and keeps skewing the plan. Check: test. Pass: both requests are refused, the first saying no watering is logged on that day, the second naming the plant as not on the list; Fern's watering of 5 days ago is still held. Conditions: plant Fern with a watering logged for 5 days ago; ask to remove Fern's entry for 4 days ago, and the entry of a plant Moss that is not on the list.

15. Statement: When the user gives a valid name of a town, the part shall take that town as the home town and replace any earlier home town. Reason: The forecast is looked up for this town; a user who moves must be able to replace it. Check: test. Pass: after the first request the home town is Oslo; after the second it is Bergen and Oslo is not held. Conditions: set the home town to Oslo, then to Bergen.

16. Statement: When the user asks for the waterings of a plant on the list, the part shall show every day logged for that plant, as logged, or say that none is logged. Reason: The user looks back to see when a plant was last watered, and to spot a mistyped entry. A plant with none must be said, so an empty answer cannot be read as a failure. Check: test. Pass: Fern's answer holds exactly the 4 days still logged; Ivy's answer says none is logged. Conditions: plant Fern with waterings on 5 distinct days, one of them removed afterwards, and plant Ivy with none.

17. Statement: When the user gives a name, a pot size, how often the plant likes water and whether it lives inside or on the balcony, and all four are valid, the part shall add a plant with those four details to the list. Reason: Nothing can be planned for a plant that is not on the list. Check: test. Pass: after the request the list holds exactly one plant, with name Fern, pot size 15 cm, interval 7 days and place inside. Conditions: start with an empty list and a valid home town; add a plant named Fern with a 15 cm pot, watered every 7 days, living inside.

18. Statement: The part shall hold the plants, the home town and the logged waterings, so that after the part is closed and opened again they are the same as when it was closed. Reason: The builder does not want to type the plants in again each time; the data lasts across days. Closed means the part ended on purpose. Check: test. Pass: the list, the home town and every plant's waterings equal what they were before closing. Conditions: add plants, set a home town, log waterings and remove one watering; close the part and open it again.

19. Statement: If where the plant lives is left out or is anything other than inside or on the balcony, then the part shall refuse the request, tell the user which entry is wrong and why, and change nothing that is stored. Reason: Only balcony plants are excused by rain, so a place the part cannot sort into one of the two would leave the rain rule undecided for that plant. Nothing but the two places is allowed, by the builder. Check: test. Pass: both bad tries are refused, naming the place and the reason, with the list unchanged; both controls are added. Conditions: try to add a plant, all else valid, with the place: nothing; garden; controls: inside and balcony.

20. Statement: While a usable forecast expects rain today, when the part works out the plants to water today, the part shall include every inside plant whose due day is today or earlier and every balcony plant whose due day is earlier than today, and no other plant, where a plant's due day is the day of its latest logged watering plus its watering interval in days, or the day the plant was added when no watering is logged. Reason: The builder excuses a balcony plant that is due today when it rains, but not one already overdue, and never an inside plant. The extra water a rained-on plant would get is the drowning the builder fears. Check: test. Pass: the plan holds the inside plant due today and both overdue plants; it does not hold the balcony plant due today, the balcony plant watered 3 days ago, or the balcony plant added today. Conditions: today fixed; the stand-in forecast gives 5 mm; interval 7 days: an inside plant and a balcony plant each watered 7 days ago (due today); an inside plant and a balcony plant each watered 9 days ago (overdue); a balcony plant watered 3 days ago; a balcony plant added today.

21. Statement: The part shall do each of its functions on a Linux laptop. Reason: The builder uses it on one Linux laptop, not a phone. Check: test. Pass: every check of this part passes on that machine. Conditions: on a Linux laptop of the builder's kind, a clean install of the part; run every other check of this part's requirements.

22. Statement: While no home town is set or no plant is on the list, when the user opens the part, the part shall tell the user which of the two, the home town or a plant, still has to be entered. Reason: On first use the builder wants to be told what to do, not an empty screen or an error. Both can be missing, so the answer names which. Check: test. Pass: the first output asks for both a home town and a plant, the second for a plant, the third for a home town; with both set, no such message is shown. Conditions: open the part with nothing set; with a home town only; with a plant only; then with both.

23. Statement: If the user gives new details for a plant that is not on the list, or details that would be refused for a new plant, then the part shall refuse the request, tell the user which entry is wrong and why, and change nothing that is stored. Reason: A change that slips through with a bad value would corrupt the schedule of a plant that exists. The same rules apply as for adding, so the same refusal is used; the builder asked for refusal, not a quiet fix. Check: test. Pass: each of the four requests is refused naming what is wrong, and Fern and Ivy hold the details they had before. Conditions: a list with plants Fern and Ivy; try to change Fern to the name Ivy; to a pot size one above 60; to an interval of nothing; try to change a plant named Moss that is not on the list.

24. Statement: If the name given for a plant is left out, consists only of spaces, or has a length outside 1 to 40 characters, then the part shall refuse the request, tell the user which entry is wrong and why, and change nothing that is stored. Reason: The name is how the user tells plants apart, so a blank one makes a plant unfindable. The limit of 40 characters and the refusal with a reason, instead of a quiet fix, are the builder's own rules. Check: test. Pass: for each of the first three tries the part shows a refusal that names the name as the wrong entry and says why, and the list is unchanged; the control is added. Conditions: a list with two plants; try to add a plant with no name; a name of only spaces; a name one character longer than 40; and, as a control, a name at exactly 40 characters with all else valid.

Reason: A half-stored change could leave a plant without its waterings, or a damaged file the builder cannot read, which is the loss of months of notes. Stopped covers closing at a bad moment, a crash and a power cut on the laptop. Check: test. Pass: after every stop, opening the part works, and the stored data equals either the state before the change or the state after it, never something between.
